subject: Performance SLO qualification — streaming & cost levers

Subject: Performance SLO qualification — streaming & cost levers

Hi Carlos / SRE team,

Thanks again for the productive call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a performance run: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary SLO: P95 first-byte latency <= 200–250 ms for interactive flows (streaming enabled).
- Peak concurrency: ~80 concurrent active users (spikes to ~120 for short windows).
- Typical request size: median ~420 tokens; 95th ~1.4–1.6k tokens.
- Streaming requirement: incremental token delivery (first-byte latency matters more than total completion time).

Immediate asks from Redwood to validate configuration and cost estimates:
1) Can you share a 1–2 hour anonymized sample of production traffic (CSV with timestamp, token_count, route)? This will let us pick batch targets and caching TTLs.
2) Confirm whether requests are prefix-heavy (many repeated instructions/prompts) — that affects KV/prefix caching wins.

What we recommend for the perf run (proposal):
- 12–24 hour perf run in a staging project using a dedicated pool.
- Runtime config: continuous batching target batch_size 12–16, prefix/KV cache enabled (TTL 1–3h), quantization profile trial q4_0 with fp16 fallback.
- Autoscale: min 2 GPUs, scale to handle 120 concurrent users at 95th.
- Streaming: chunking at ~128 tokens per chunk to balance latency and throughput.

Attachments: redwood_perf_playbook.pdf (playbook + checklist), 20260303-Sable-perf-estimates.xlsx (rough estimate matrix).

Next steps:
- If you can share the sample traffic and confirm permission for a staging perf run, we’ll schedule the run and a follow-up 30–45 minute sync to review results and recommended Dedicated configuration (pool size, quantization, routing policies).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi / Vivek for engineering validation once we have the sample.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifications from our side before we hand over traffic: 

- The P95 target is firm at 200 ms for first-byte for the main patient-facing flow. For background jobs (batch reranks) latency is looser and not streaming-critical.
- Peak concurrency: 80 sustained, plus ~120 for bursts (1–2 min). We need to make sure tail latency during bursts stays within SLO.
- Token distribution: median ~420, mean ~550, 95th ~1600, max ~2400 (rare).
- Prefix reuse: yes — about ~30% of requests share common system prompts and fixed prefixes for instruction templates.

Two questions: 
1) What kind of latency trade-off should we expect if we move to q4_0 quantization vs fp16? We care more about tail latency than a 5–10% cost saving if it increases the P95.
2) Can prefix/KV caching reduce costs significantly given our 30% reuse?

Happy to share an anonymized hour of traffic and the procurement contact Lina (copied) will coordinate NDA/procurement questions. We’d like a short demo of streaming behavior if possible — seeing first-byte timings live will help.

Carlos — thanks for the clarifications. Below are more concrete expectations and tradeoffs based on similar customers and our internal benchmarks. I’ve attached the perf estimates spreadsheet for reference.

Quick answers to your questions:
- q4_0 vs fp16: q4_0 typically reduces memory and inference cost by ~40–60% on our runtime for 13B-class models. Latency impact depends on kernel and hardware; in many configs p50 stays similar and p95 increases 5–15 ms depending on sequence length. Since you prioritize P95, we recommend testing q4_0 with strict p95 monitoring and an fp16 fallback for requests that hit tail thresholds.
- Prefix/KV caching: with ~30% prefix reuse, expected token-level cost reduction is ~20–45% (depends on how much of response is cached vs generated). Caching also improves first-byte latency for cached prefixes dramatically (often 2–5x faster).

Recommended perf-run config (we propose to run this in your staging project):
- Model variant: open-13b (fp16) + open-13b-q4_0 (trial) as fallback routing.
- Quantization profile: q4_0 for steady-state cost benefit; autoswitch to fp16 for specific endpoints if p95 > 200 ms.
- Continuous batching: target batch_size 12–16 (reduces per-token cost while keeping first-byte latency under control).
- KV/prefix caching: enable with TTL 3h, target cache hit rate >=25% during test.
- Streaming: chunk size 128 tokens; enable immediate first-chunk delivery.
- Dedicated pool sizing (initial): 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (autoscale policy to burst to 6 for short windows).
- Concurrency cap: 200 soft cap per pool with queuing/priority for interactive routes.

Estimated outcomes (from modelled traffic in spreadsheet):
- With batching + q4_0 + caching, estimated unit cost reduction 38–52% vs fp16 no-cache baseline.
- Expected P95 with recommended config: ~160–220 ms for first-byte on 420-token median; tail up to ~300 ms on 95th token-length without fallback.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the anonymized 1–2 hour traffic (CSV) and confirm permission for a 12–24 hour staging perf run.
2) We run perf test, return a results dashboard and cost/latency breakdown, then align on Dedicated sizing and rollout policy.
3) Optional: we can run an A/B of q4_0 vs fp16 (same routing) to capture real delta under your workloads.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute results review after the run. Lina — looping you for procurement/NDAs.

Best,
Marissa
